I'm 72 years old, and I've been farming these fields in Quzhou since I was a teenager. My father farmed here before me, and his father before him. I only went to primary school, but I know this land better than any book could teach me. I have about 3 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain.

This year, I'll stick to what has always fed my family and put a little money in my pocket: the wheat-maize double crop system. That's how we do it here. In early October, I'll sow winter wheat. I can't afford to gamble with fancy new things at my age. After the wheat harvest in early June, I'll immediately plant summer maize. Every day matters in that gap.

For the wheat, I'll use an improved variety — the seed shop in town sells Jimai seeds that my neighbors and I have used for years. They perform well here. For the maize, I'll use hybrid seed. You have to use hybrid corn these days; everyone does, and the yield difference is too big to ignore.

Fertilizer? I'll put down compound fertilizer as base dressing and top-dress with urea. The wheat needs more nitrogen — I'll give it about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus about 6 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium. For the maize, I'll do around 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I learned long ago that skimping on fertilizer means skimping on dinner.

I'll irrigate the wheat three times: once when it greens up in spring, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. The maize I'll irrigate twice — after sowing if it's dry, and again at the big trumpet stage. I rely on the village pumping station; water is life here.

Pest control? I'll spray twice for each crop — herbicide early, then one spray for insects and disease when I see them coming. I walk my fields every morning; I spot trouble before it spreads.

For tillage, I'll use rotary tillage. It's faster and easier on my old bones than deep ploughing, and it works fine for these crops.

I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat and about 550 kg per mu from the maize. If the weather cooperates, that should see me through another year.
